method.kind: Review versioned ezdxf API/FAQ documentation, PyPI artifact metadata, acis-core documentation, current cq-acis geometry limits, and the local generator/handoff
method.limitations: No candidate was installed or executed. API and package metadata establish discovery and artifact-selection details only, not generated ACDSDATA bytes, libdxfrw round-trip behavior, B-rep validity, or native CAD acceptance. The exact PyPI wheel has a checksum but is not marked Trusted Publishing. Current cq-acis main documentation is mutable; docs.rs acis-core 0.3.11 and PyPI cq-acis 0.3.12 are not assumed to be a matched dependency set.

sources.revision: Stable documentation identifies itself as ezdxf 1.4.5; accessed 2026-10-18
sources.observed: The detailed ACIS API documents body_from_mesh(MeshBuilder), export_dxf() to ACIS-based DXF entities, and export_sab() with ACIS 21800 sufficient for R2013/R2018. Closed meshes create solid bodies; separate meshes can become separate lumps unless split before body construction. The FAQ says SAT-only/no creation, but its preamble labels it the old FAQ with new entries moved elsewhere after late 2023.
sources.limits: The documented writer is limited to simple known structures and polyhedra; ezdxf has no ACIS kernel, unsupported parsed entities may be lost, and the API guide's statement that Autodesk/BricsCAD load examples is not an executed acceptance result for this exact artifact.

sources.observed: The wheel SHA-256 is e78a6b6aaac31f915026694f669cb3172636380caad9ec41007636f034013106. PyPI metadata reports Trusted Publishing: No.
sources.limits: The digest is useful for byte-exact repeatability, but no publisher attestation or source commit identity was established. This wheel was not downloaded or installed.

sources.revision: docs.rs acis-core 0.3.11; PyPI cq-acis 0.3.12; current cq-acis geometry guide on mutable main, accessed 2026-10-18
sources.observed: acis-core documents an experimental source-free SAB author for one axis-aligned Asm23200MetricBox and states that reference closure does not prove B-rep validity or compatibility with a particular ASM version. cq-acis uses a shared model API with acis-core and converts supported models through CadQuery/OpenCascade. The reviewed package/docs versions were not established as a matching release dependency set.
sources.limits: This is a bounded experimental author/parser family, not a DXF/AcDs writer or independent parser/kernel vote. OCCT geometry is shared-kernel evidence with FreeCAD, not an independent-kernel result. Mutable main docs may include unreleased work.

sources.observed: The helper builds one ACIS 218 polyhedral 3DSOLID at a time, currently with dimensions (5, 7, 11), writes an AC1027 DXF and a separate SAB file, and performs an ezdxf same-library version/entity/carrier equality self-check. Its module documentation explicitly says it does not create a DWG or ACDSDATA section. ezdxf is unavailable in the currently selected Python environment.
sources.limits: The helper is not the proposed two-body asymmetric manifest generator and cannot by itself validate ACDSDATA/key association, libdxfrw conversion, independent geometry, or native acceptance. Its dependency hint is not an exact artifact pin. No attempt was made to install ezdxf or run the helper.

assessment.planImpact: Treat the ezdxf 1.4.5 detailed API as a concrete optional source-from-scratch polyhedron producer candidate, with the old FAQ discrepancy retained but chronologically qualified. At the existing composed 3D checkpoint, hash-pin and isolate the exact artifact, author two separate analytic 3DSOLID bodies, inspect actual AC1027 ACDSDATA/SAB payloads and per-entity associations, and then exercise the local conversion chain. The current one-body helper is not enough. Keep acis-core/cq-acis as one experimental project-family route; do not count shared OCCT or reference closure as an independent semantic/native pass. If optional external routes are unavailable, mark those stages not run and continue local implementation.
